home_self_description.quote: The Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, or C2PA, provides an open technical standard for publishers, creators and consumers to establish the origin and edits of digital content. It's called Content Credentials, and it ensures content complies with standards as the digital ecosystem evolves.

nutrition_label.quote: Content Credentials function like a nutrition label for digital content, giving a peek at the content's history available for anyone to access, at any time.

operator.quote: Copyright © Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, established as a Joint Development Foundation Projects, LLC, Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity Series.

provenance_purpose.quote: Provenance empowers content creators and editors, regardless of their geographic location or degree of access to technology, to disclose information about how an asset was created, how it was changed and what was changed.

opt_in.quote: It is designed to enable global, opt-in, adoption of digital provenance techniques

regulators.quote: It is also possible that regulatory bodies and governmental agencies could utilize this specification to establish standards for digital provenance.

scope.quote: This specification describes the technical aspects of the C2PA architecture; a model for storing and accessing cryptographically verifiable information whose trustworthiness can be assessed based on a defined trust model .

no_value_judgment.quote: C2PA specifications SHOULD NOT provide value judgments about whether a given set of provenance data is 'good' or 'bad,' merely whether the assertions included within can be validated as associated with the underlying asset, correctly formed, and free from tampering.

assertions.quote: These statements, called assertions, make up the provenance of a given asset and represent a series of trust signals that can be used by a human to improve their view of trustworthiness concerning the asset.

claim_signed.quote: This claim is digitally signed by the claim generator on behalf of the signer , using the signer's signing credential, producing the claim signature.

trust_basis.quote: The basis of making trust decisions in C2PA, our trust model , is the identity of the signer associated with the cryptographic signing key used to sign a claim in a C2PA Manifest.

actor.quote: A human or non-human (hardware or software) that is participating in the C2PA ecosystem. For example: a camera (capture device), image editing software, cloud service or the person using such tools.

claim_generator.quote: The non-human (hardware or software) actor that generates the claim about an asset as well as the claim signature , thus leading to the asset 's associated C2PA Manifest .

signer.quote: The credential holder of a private key that is used to sign the claim . The signer is identified by the subject of the credential.

assertion_def.quote: A data structure which represents a statement either made (or "created") by the signer or simply gathered at claim generation-time, concerning the asset .

authenticity_def.quote: A property of digital content comprising a set of facts (such as the provenance data and hard bindings ) that can be cryptographically verified as not having been tampered with.

created_attributed.quote: All created_assertions are attributed to the signer as the Trust Model is rooted in the trust of the signer.

gathered_not_attributed.quote: By putting an assertion into this list, the claim generator is declaring that the assertion is part of the claim, but it was not sourced from the claim generator and is not attributed to the signer. For example, assertions containing information entered by a human actor would be listed in gathered_assertions .

consumer_decides.quote: In dashed lines, below, is the consumer (who is not specified in the trust model), who uses the identity of the signer, along with other trust signals, to decide whether the assertions made about an asset are true.

validator_conclusions.quote: The actor consuming the asset, usually through their user agent and its user interface, then has to interpret those statements to arrive at a set of conclusions of their own about the provenance of the asset they are consuming.

manifest_states.quote: Any Trusted manifest is also Valid, and any Valid manifest is also Well-Formed.

valid_attributed.quote: If a C2PA Manifest is Valid, then the manifest's claim can be attributed to the claim generator which is identified by the claim_generator_info field of the claim

display_warning.quote: a warning that the data shall not be attributed to the manifest's signer,

metadata_attribution.quote: Having the metadata in an assertion establishes that the metadata in that assertion is significant, because it has been explicitly included in the C2PA Manifest, and signed by a specific signer - thus enabling cryptographic validation and attribution of the data.

custom_metadata.quote: Custom labelled metadata assertions can contain any values from any schemas.

dc_subset.quote: Only the following Dublin Core ( dc ) properties are supported: dc:coverage dc:date dc:format dc:identifier dc:language dc:relation dc:type

actors_removed.quote: ; NOTE: an earlier version of this specification also included an "actors" field, however this was removed in version 2.0.

digital_source_type.quote: For all assets, a corresponding digitalSourceType field, with an appropriate value, shall be recorded with the c2pa.created action, to indicate the nature of the asset at its inception.

genai_example.quote: EXAMPLE: A generative AI model generates a video in response to a text prompt. aim.quote: As AI writing tools become widespread, we need to understand how both humans and machines evaluate literary style, a domain where objective standards are elusive and judgments are inherently subjective.

materials.quote: We conducted controlled experiments using Raymond Queneau's Exercises in Style (1947) to measure attribution bias across evaluators.

study1.quote: Study 1 compared human participants (N=556) and AI models (N=13) evaluating literary passages from Queneau versus GPT-4-generated versions under three conditions: blind, accurately labeled, and counterfactually labeled.

study2.quote: Study 2 tested bias generalization across a 14x14 matrix of AI evaluators and creators.

finding.quote: Both studies revealed systematic pro-human attribution bias.

effect_sizes.quote: Humans showed +13.7 percentage point (pp) bias (Cohen's h = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.19-0.37), while AI models showed +34.3 percentage point bias (h = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.62-0.78), a 2.5-fold stronger effect (P<0.001).

study2_result.quote: Study 2 confirmed this bias operates across AI architectures (+25.8pp, 95% CI: 24.1-27.6%), demonstrating that AI systems systematically devalue creative content when labeled as "AI-generated" regardless of which AI created it.

inversion.quote: We also find that attribution labels lead evaluators to invert assessment criteria, with identical features receiving opposing evaluations based solely on perceived authorship.

suggestion.quote: This suggests AI models have absorbed human cultural biases against artificial creativity during training, including through the preference signals on which they are aligned.

claim.quote: Our study represents the first controlled comparison of attribution bias between human and artificial evaluators in aesthetic judgment, revealing that AI systems not only replicate but amplify this human tendency.

relations.note: both test how a stated human or AI label shifts readers' judgment of literary texts; Porter and Machery report that participants rated poems lower when told they were AI-generated; the halo abstract does not cite Porter and Machery

aim.quote: This study examined whether non-expert readers could reliably differentiate between AI-generated poems and those written by well-known human poets.

more_human.quote: Notably, participants were more likely to judge AI-generated poems as human-authored than actual human-authored poems

study2.quote: We recruited a new sample of 696 participants from Prolific.

self_description.quote: Exploring the opportunities and challenges of frontier technologies in an interconnected world

operator.quote: At WIPO, the IP and Frontier Technologies Division, in close collaboration with the IP Futures and Knowledge Management Section, facilitates discussion and knowledge building among Member States and stakeholders on how frontier technologies interact with IP, supporting well‑informed policy choices.

human_focus.quote: The IP system that we have today was developed with a focus on human creation and innovation

conversation_reach_2.quote: Over the last 5 years, almost 12’000 people have participated in the WIPO Conversation, from 172 countries
